plan: First playable: 12 constellations on a dark sky chart where the next star glows and a tap draws the line, ending with the voiced figure and one real star fact. Free-form drawing and a full sky map are left out.
First playable: 8 desk layouts from 2x2 to 4x4 pairing each planet with its moon card, voiced names and a short fact on each match, no timer. Scoring, dwarf planets and exoplanets are deferred.

First playable: 24 puzzles where one swipe gives a comet an impulse at a chosen moment and the projected orbit redraws, showing that early small pushes beat late big ones. Multi-body chaos and a level editor are left out.
First playable: 15 landing sites on the Moon with a throttle and tilt control, a visible fuel gauge and an assist mode that slows gravity. Other bodies, docking and terrain generation are left out.

First playable: a sandbox where dragging sets a planet starting velocity and traced ellipses reveal Kepler laws, plus 20 garden challenges such as making a round orbit. Moons of moons and save sharing are deferred.

First playable: one calm station display where delayed telescope readings arrive on a timeline and the player predicts where tracked objects will be, over 15 shifts. Multiple stations and real survey data are deferred.

First playable: a workbench with about 20 modules where the player assembles a probe within a mass budget, sees the rocket equation result and flies it on 20 short missions. Custom parts and 3D views are left out.

First playable: one space board where each move travels as a visible light signal so both sides act on old information, with a kind AI and 15 scenario puzzles. Online play and large maps are deferred.

First playable: a pannable and zoomable star field built from a real catalog with 20 guided tours that ask the child to find objects and show their distance in light-years. Deep-sky photography and AR are left out.
First playable: 20 navigation challenges where the player rotates a solar sail so sunlight slowly bends the probe path toward a target orbit. Planetary flybys and mission planning tools are deferred.

First playable: a globe view where the player places satellites on a few orbit types, links them to cover isolated ground stations and watches message delay, across 24 coverage puzzles. Launch costs and 3D globes are deferred.

First playable: a 3D rocket assembly bay with about 25 parts and a staging panel showing delta-v, then a flight to orbit around one planet over 20 missions. Other planets, docking and crew are left out.

First playable: one 3D fictional planet whose atmosphere, star distance and sunlight sliders change temperature, oceans and ice, with 15 habitability goals. Evolving life, civilizations and multiple stars are deferred.

First playable: a 3D cockpit flight between a home station and nearby beacons where speed sliders show time dilation, Doppler color and aberration, with clocks compared on return over 30 legs. Free-form galaxy travel is left out.

First playable: 18 docking runs where tiny reaction-control puffs align a capsule with a rotating ring, with a relative-velocity readout and a calm practice mode. 3D views and fuel economy campaigns are deferred.

First playable: 12 short rescue sweeps where a drone uses tractor-field arcs to push drifting debris aside and reach stranded probes, choosing which to save first. Upgrades trees and endless mode are left out.

First playable: a side-view rover driving over generated terrain to 12 outcrops, sampling rocks and comparing instrument readings with an uncertainty bar to sort rock types. Full 3D Mars maps are deferred.
